This project analyzes air quality data from 2018, 2019, and 2020 containing measurements of carbon monoxide (CO), particulate matter (PM2.5), and ozone (O₃). The data were cleaned, combined, summarized, and visualized to examine yearly and seasonal patterns in pollutant concentrations.

----------------------------------------------------------------
```{r}
# ----------------------------------------------------------------

# 1. Load packages
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(gt)



```

# Data Processing 

The process_air_quality() function was created to clean and process each yearly air quality dataset. 
The function imports the data from the CSV files, renames pollutant variables to shorter names (CO, PM25, and O3), converts the date variable to date format (month, day, year), removes duplicate records, replaces negative pollutant concentrations with zero, averages observations recorded on the same day, and returns a cleaned dataset containing one row per day.

----------------------------------------------------------------
```{r}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------

# 2. Create processing function

#Function to clean and process yearly air quality dataset


# Arguments:
  #   file_path = location of csv file
  #   ozone_unit = "ppm" (default) or "ppb"
  #
  # Returns:
  #   Clean tibble of daily pollutant measurements

#---------------------------------------------------

process_air_quality <- function(file,
                                ozone_unit = "ppm") {
  
  air <- read_csv(file,
                  show_col_types = FALSE)
  
  air_clean <- air %>%
  
  #rename variables to create simplicity when using variable names during coding
    rename(
      CO = `Daily Max 8-hour CO Concentration`,
      PM25 = `Daily Mean PM2.5 Concentration`,
      O3 = `Daily Max 8-hour Ozone Concentration`
    ) %>%
    
   #convert date variable 
    mutate(
      Date = mdy(Date)
    ) %>%
    
  #remove duplicate measurements 
    distinct()
  
  pollutants <- c("CO", "PM25", "O3")
  
  for(var in pollutants){
  
  #take care of negative values by setting them equal to zero
    air_clean[[var]] <- ifelse(
      air_clean[[var]] < 0,
      0,
      air_clean[[var]]
    )
  }
  
  air_clean <- air_clean %>%
    
    group_by(Date) %>%
    
  #find average of duplicate entries
    summarise(
      CO = ifelse(all(is.na(CO)), NA, mean(CO, na.rm = TRUE)),
      PM25 = ifelse(all(is.na(PM25)), NA, mean(PM25, na.rm = TRUE)),
      O3 = ifelse(all(is.na(O3)), NA, mean(O3, na.rm = TRUE)),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  
  #convert ozone units to ppb
  
  if(ozone_unit == "ppb"){
    
    air_clean <- air_clean %>%
      mutate(O3 = O3 * 1000)
    
  }
  
  return(air_clean)
}

```


```{r}
# ----------------------------------------------------------------

# 3. Process each dataset

aq2018 <- process_air_quality("AQ_2018.csv")

aq2019 <- process_air_quality("AQ_2019.csv")

aq2020 <- process_air_quality("AQ_2020.csv")

```


```{r, include=FALSE}
# ----------------------------------------------------------------


# 4. Combine datasets


#Add year variable 
aq2018 <- aq2018 %>%
  mutate(Year = 2018)

aq2019 <- aq2019 %>%
  mutate(Year = 2019)

aq2020 <- aq2020 %>%
  mutate(Year = 2020)


#combine data 
aq_all <- bind_rows(
  aq2018,
  aq2019,
  aq2020
)


#Add month labels  
aq_all <- aq_all %>%
  mutate(
    Month = month(Date),
    Month_Name = month(Date,
                       label = TRUE,
                       abbr = TRUE)
  )


#Checking table contents

glimpse(aq_all)


#checking rows and missingness

nrow(aq2018)
nrow(aq2019)
nrow(aq2020)

sum(is.na(aq_all$CO))
sum(is.na(aq_all$PM25))
sum(is.na(aq_all$O3))
```
----------------------------------------------------------------

# Summary tables

```{r, include=FALSE}
# ----------------------------------------------------------------


# 5. Create yearly summary tables

create_summary_table <- function(data, year_label){
  
#Find min and max of CO, PM2.5, and O3
  data %>%
    summarise(
      `CO Min (ppm)` = min(CO, na.rm = TRUE),
      `CO Max (ppm)` = max(CO, na.rm = TRUE),
      
      `PM2.5 Min (ug/m3)` = min(PM25, na.rm = TRUE),
      `PM2.5 Max (ug/m3)` = max(PM25, na.rm = TRUE),
      
      `O3 Min (ppm)` = min(O3, na.rm = TRUE),
      `O3 Max (ppm)` = max(O3, na.rm = TRUE)
    ) %>%
  
  #Produce cleaner table format 
    pivot_longer(
      everything(),
      names_to = "Measure",
      values_to = "Value"
    ) %>%
    
    gt() %>%
    
  #Rounding decimals 
  
    fmt_number(
      columns = Value,
      decimals = 3
    ) %>%
    
    tab_header(
      title = paste(
        "Minimum and Maximum Daily Pollutant Concentrations:",
        year_label
      )
    )
}



#Create tables for all 3 measurements 

table2018 <- create_summary_table(
  filter(aq_all, Year == 2018),
  "2018"
)

table2019 <- create_summary_table(
  filter(aq_all, Year == 2019),
  "2019"
)

table2020 <- create_summary_table(
  filter(aq_all, Year == 2020),
  "2020"
)



```


```{r}
#outputting tables
table2018

table2019

table2020

```

# Plot 1 
```{r, include=FALSE}

# 6. Create Plot 1

#select only month name, co, and o3
plot1_data <- aq_all %>%
  select(Month_Name, CO, O3) %>%
  
#putting co and 03 under categories
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(CO, O3),
    names_to = "Pollutant",
    values_to = "Concentration"
  ) %>%
  
  group_by(Month_Name, Pollutant) %>%
  

  #calculating Confidence Intervals
  summarise(
    mean = mean(Concentration, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(Concentration, na.rm = TRUE),
    n = sum(!is.na(Concentration)),
    se = sd / sqrt(n),
    
    lower = mean - 1.96 * se,
    upper = mean + 1.96 * se,
    
    .groups = "drop"
  )

head(plot1_data)


#plot the monthly average CO and O3 with confidence intervals

plot1 <- ggplot(
  plot1_data,
  aes(
    x = Month_Name,
    y = mean,
    color = Pollutant,
    group = Pollutant
  )
) +
  geom_line(size = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper),
    width = 0.2
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~Pollutant, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    title = "Monthly Average CO and O3 Concentrations",
    x = "Month",
    y = "Mean Concentration"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 45,
      hjust = 1,
      vjust = 1
    )
  )




```


```{r, fig.width=10, fig.height=5}

#output plot 1

plot1

```


The CO and O₃ concentrations were displayed separately because the pollutants are measured on  different concentration ranges. Using separate scales makes the seasonal patterns of both pollutants easier to see and prevents the smaller O₃ values from being overshadowed by the larger CO values.

# Plot 2
```{r}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------


# 7. Create Plot 2

#group by year and month since these are the values of interest
plot2_data <- aq_all %>%
  group_by(Year, Month_Name) %>%
  summarise(
    mean = mean(PM25, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(PM25, na.rm = TRUE),
    n = sum(!is.na(PM25)),
    se = sd / sqrt(n),
    
    lower = mean - 1.96 * se,
    upper = mean + 1.96 * se,
    
    .groups = "drop"
  )


#create plot for monthly avg PM2.5 per year

plot2 <- ggplot(
  plot2_data,
  aes(
    x = Month_Name,
    y = mean,
    color = factor(Year),
    group = Year
  )
) +
  
  geom_line(size = 1) +
  
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(
      ymin = lower,
      ymax = upper
    ),
    width = 0.20
  ) +
  
  labs(
    title = "Monthly Average PM2.5 Concentrations by Year",
    x = "Month",
    y = "Mean PM2.5 Concentration (µg/m³)",
    color = "Year"
  ) +
  
  theme_minimal()

plot2
```

A line plot was used because it effectively displays changes in monthly PM2.5 concentrations over time and displays comparisons across years, while error bars show the precision of the estimated means.

----------------------------------------------------------------
# Table & Plot Interpretations

The monthly average plots for CO and O3 showed noticeable seasonal trends, where CO reached the highest averages during the winter months, and O3 averaging the most during summer months.On the other hand, PM2.5 showed a variety of patterns between the months for each year.These differences can be seen between 2018 and 2019, but there was only 121 days of data available for the year 2020.
